prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1073; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a sideswipe during a lane change. The insured's vehicle was struck on the driver's side while merging, and the claimant reports a wrist fracture from the impact. The claimant is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is named on it, so coverage for this vehicle and driver is in place. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos from the scene match the account given by the other driver.

Entry 4: Spoke with the claimant, who described the lane change and impact the same way as in the initial report. The account has stayed consistent across every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage is mostly in line with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is on record, and the repair estimate has been sent to the body shop for review.

Entry 6: Medical records show the wrist fracture was treated along a typical course, with follow-up visits tapering off as the claimant improved. Whether the fracture was caused by this crash is still unclear and needs further medical review.

Entry 7: Claimant mentioned a minor strain in the same area years ago, which healed completely according to the prior records requested. Noted for the medical review, with no current evidence it affects this claim.

Entry 8: Witness statements, photos and the other driver's account all confirm the accident happened as described. Liability review is underway based on these sources.

Entry 9: File is pending the medical causation review and the final repair figures. Will reassess once the treating provider's report is received.
